check.catches:
Agreement-target records: what an agreement claim is compared with, and how.

An agreement claim of the pinned request plan names its comparison only as a target class,
a locator, a metric and a tolerance. ``inputs/agreement_targets.json`` adds one target
record per agreement claim: the reference kind and its pins, the result and reference
quantities with any declared conversion, the reference family, the node lattice, the
tolerance rule and a noise-model reference. One claim has one target; a second comparator
is a second agreement claim. The structure is ``data/claims/agreement_target.schema.json``.

This module is a CHECK-IN 1 section provider registered in ``data/checkin/sections.json``.
``checkin_section`` renders the ``agreement_targets`` section, including each target's
node coverage of its reference lattice, into the CHECK-IN 1 bytes; ``checkin_errors``
refuses a CHECK-IN 1 whose agreement claim has no valid target record. Consumers (residual
diagnosis, recipe ledger, calibration, review rows) read ``targets(rundir)``.

check.catches:
Compare SimpleAnalysis/Delphes acceptance times efficiency with published maps.

This checks point-estimate agreement for the complete generation, shower,
detector and selection chain. It does not isolate a detector defect, justify
retuning, propagate MC/published uncertainties, or establish statistical coverage.
Normalization cancellation requires the same generated-process and decay basis.

Input: SimpleAnalysis CSV (SR,events,acceptance,err) or a per-SR JSON object.
The selected-event yield is preserved as a real number for weighted samples.
Nonfinite/negative values, duplicate CSV regions and invalid denominators fail.
The CSV err column is not propagated; reports explicitly state this limitation.

Published A×ε comes from an explicit acceptance-times-efficiency table, or from
separate acceptance and efficiency tables at matching lookup nodes. Acceptance
alone is not an A×ε reference. --acc-unit-scale applies only to separate acceptance
tables; the default 1e-3 convention must match the particular HEPData publication.
The second grid axis is a splitting: pass --dm or --m-lsp, never both.

Lookup: node within 1e-6 GeV; local 1-D interpolation with a bounded span; otherwise
NEAREST for diagnosis only. A nearest-node driving comparison cannot pass even
inside the outer grid boundary. Interpolation uncertainty is not estimated.

Driving regions are the most occupied bins and bins within --driving-factor,
or explicit --driving-sr-override choices. Occupancy is a validation heuristic,
not an inferred ordering of statistical sensitivity. Tails are report-only.
All requested rows remain in the comparison counts. The worst residual is the
maximum over every driving row. Missing driving references/yields, no driving
region, or unmatched driving references fail. Zero acceptance is a real deficit.

The legacy mu95_impact name denotes an acceptance residual proxy, not a limit
uncertainty. inverse_signal_limit_shift reports conditional 1/ratio - 1 algebra
for uniform signal rescaling only. Similar residuals across regions trigger a
normalization/efficiency diagnostic prompt; they do not establish a physical cause.

Exit code 0 means a report was produced; consumers MUST read its PASS/WARN/FAIL
verdict. Parse/validation errors exit nonzero. Output is Markdown + JSON.

Example:
  certify_acceptance.py --acceptance <routine>.txt --tables-dir HEPData-yaml
      --grid slepton --m-parent 200 --dm 50 --srs SR_S_iMT2a,SR_S_high_iMT2a
      --out acceptance-certification.md

retuning, propagate MC/published uncertainties, or establish statistical coverage.
Normalization cancellation requires the same generated-process and decay basis.

Input: SimpleAnalysis CSV (SR,events,acceptance,err) or a per-SR JSON object.
The selected-event yield is preserved as a real number for weighted samples.
Nonfinite/negative values, duplicate CSV regions and invalid denominators fail.
The CSV err column is not propagated; reports explicitly state this limitation.

Published A×ε comes from an explicit acceptance-times-efficiency table, or from
separate acceptance and efficiency tables at matching lookup nodes. Acceptance
alone is not an A×ε reference. --acc-unit-scale applies only to separate acceptance
tables; the default 1e-3 convention must match the particular HEPData publication.
The second grid axis is a splitting: pass --dm or --m-lsp, never both.

Lookup: node within 1e-6 GeV; local 1-D interpolation with a bounded span; otherwise
NEAREST for diagnosis only. A nearest-node driving comparison cannot pass even
inside the outer grid boundary. Interpolation uncertainty is not estimated.

Driving regions are the most occupied bins and bins within --driving-factor,
or explicit --driving-sr-override choices. Occupancy is a validation heuristic,
not an inferred ordering of statistical sensitivity. Tails are report-only.
All requested rows remain in the comparison counts. The worst residual is the
maximum over every driving row. Missing driving references/yields, no driving
region, or unmatched driving references fail. Zero acceptance is a real deficit.

The legacy mu95_impact name denotes an acceptance residual proxy, not a limit
uncertainty. inverse_signal_limit_shift reports conditional 1/ratio - 1 algebra
for uniform signal rescaling only. Similar residuals across regions trigger a
normalization/efficiency diagnostic prompt; they do not establish a physical cause.

Exit code 0 means a report was produced; consumers MUST read its PASS/WARN/FAIL
verdict. Parse/validation errors exit nonzero. Output is Markdown + JSON.

Example:
  certify_acceptance.py --acceptance <routine>.txt --tables-dir HEPData-yaml
      --grid slepton --m-parent 200 --dm 50 --srs SR_S_iMT2a,SR_S_high_iMT2a
      --out acceptance-certification.md

check.catches:
G8 conformance: census of every agent call site.

Every ``.py`` file under ``src/ravel`` is parsed with ``ast``. Import aliases, literal
``getattr(module, "name")``, simple local bindings, parameter annotations and
same-module constructor helpers are resolved, and each call site is recorded at
function granularity (``module:qualname``) under one of seven sinks:

- S1 model reach: ``AgentHost.execute``, ``provider_transport.request``, the
  ``cli_agent_host`` entry points, a process launch whose argv names a model CLI
  launcher from ``data/transports``, and generic HTTP clients;
- S2 orchestration: LangGraph ``StateGraph``/``compile``/``Send``/``interrupt``/
  ``Command``/``ToolNode``/``create_react_agent``/``entrypoint``/``task``;
- S3 role dispatch: ``agent_graph``, ``research_cycle.execute_graph``, ``agent_worker``;
- S4 provider SDK imports and S5 upstream agent loops (direct or ``import_module``);
- S6 instruction literals under an ``"instructions"`` key;
- S7 calls to ``data/graphs/consequential_sinks.json``.

Sanctions name qualnames, never whole modules (``data/agents/sanctioned.json``). An
S7 call inside an ``effect`` body that names one of the sink's gates is ``substrate``.
Everything else is a ``bypass`` and must appear in ``data/agents/bypass_baseline.json``
with the package that removes it. The baseline only shrinks; its ``enforcement`` is
``report`` (W4), ``block_new`` (W-a) or ``empty`` (W-e, the G8 pass condition).

Syntactic detection is not coverage: the mutation fixtures measure recall and the
runtime tripwire (``workflow/agent_tripwire.py``) catches dynamic paths.

    python -m ravel.validation.check_agent_paths census [--write | --check]
    python -m ravel.validation.check_agent_paths report
    ravel release check --gate G8 [--mode report|block_new|empty] [--out FILE]

check.catches:
Agent-surface consistency gate: the routing/docs/skills layer must be mechanically coherent.

The failure class this catches: a fresh cheap-model session routed by CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md into
files that disagree, 404, or contradict each other. Run it per session (fast, stdlib-only,
read-only); the pre-commit hook runs it with --stage:

  check_agent_surface.py                # this tree's checks
  check_agent_surface.py --stage DIR    # ALSO: dead-reference check over a copy of the tree
  check_agent_surface.py --public       # public-tree mode (automatic in this repository)
  check_agent_surface.py --project DIR  # a project with an installed RAVEL agent surface

The development route is CONTRIBUTING.md -> DIRECTORY.md unless an optional settings file
declares another (`development_route`); only the documents the tree carries are checked.
Public mode also rejects routing docs that name material outside the distribution selection.

Checks (each PASS/FAIL, exit 1 on any FAIL):
  fork        CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md agree: physicist route -> docs/workflow/start.md; the
              development read order is the configured one, in order
  refs        every backticked path in the routing docs / workflow docs / skills EXISTS
  skills      every SKILL.md has valid frontmatter (name == dir, trigger-rich description)
  mirror      .claude/skills <-> .agents/skills byte-identical (single source: sync_skills.py)
  dirmap      every DIRECTORY.md table path exists (local-only rows may name gitignored paths); unmapped top-level entries reported (WARN)
  readiness   readiness percentages quoted in the routing docs equal the committed audit report
  stepcount   'N steps' claims across routing docs == the actual count of docs/workflow/steps/*.md
  hygiene     no trial-run tokens in docs/workflow/ + .claude/skills + .claude/rules + README
  handbooks   runtime tool handbooks (src/ravel/data/skills/tools): closed six-key frontmatter,
              token budget (--token-budget, line proxy), pitfalls name a RAVEL check or are
              advisory, parameters are listed operation.field paths, upstream versions match the
              toolchain manifest and Python pins, review records list the tested code blocks
  installed   (--installed DIR) installed handbook copies are byte-identical to the package
  skill-keys  report-only: workflow skills using frontmatter keys outside the six-key set
  collisions  report-only: skill descriptions that overlap strongly
  stage       (--stage) every path referenced by files IN the stage exists IN the stage

  --doctor-report FILE prints the handbook unavailable ledger from a `ravel doctor --json` (or
  native_doctor) report.

check.catches:
Generality gate: the repository names no specific analysis, challenge, person or showcase point.

One scan, run by the pre-commit hook, the public-scope export check and the development
snapshot push. It reports four classes of finding:

(a) named challenges, benchmark or evaluation suites and compared agent systems;
(b) specific analysis identifiers: experiment analysis codes and notes, Rivet routine ids,
    search-specific routine names, experiment-year slugs, arXiv, INSPIRE and HEPData record ids
    and physics-journal DOIs;
(c) person names;
(d) benchmark points tied to one study.

The (b) shapes are structural patterns. Names, which no pattern can recognise, come from a
maintained denylist that stores only keyed digests of each term's letters and digits, so the
list itself names nothing. A text matches an entry when a run of its words, joined without
separators and lower-cased, has the entry's digest: "Fable Quarry", "FableQuarry",
"fable_quarry" and "FABLE-QUARRY" are one entry. Two outside lists join the denylist at run
time: the term list in RAVEL_EVAL_TERMS_FILE / RAVEL_EVAL_TERMS, and the fingerprints and
document hashes of the owner's restricted-source list in RAVEL_RESTRICTED_SOURCES.

(e) placeholder identifiers: an arXiv-shaped number whose year-month field no real number has,
    an analysis label of the form ANA-9<nnn>-<nn>, a routine label of the form Routine00<n>, and
    any DOI, link or report number built from them. A placeholder that stands where a source
    should be cited is a fabricated citation, so these are refused in every file.

Upstream sources are cited, not named: the citation list (data/generality/citations.json) gives,
for each file that cites the source of shipped data, a method, a convention or a tool, the exact
identifiers that file may carry. Those strings are removed from the file's text before the scan,
so any other identifier in the same file is a finding, the same identifier in a file that is not
listed is a finding, and a listed identifier that its file no longer carries is a finding too
(stale-citation). The list never applies to the placeholder rules.

The allowlist is empty. A supplied allowlist ({path: [rule, ...]}) must match exactly; a stale
entry is itself a finding. Output names the path, line and rule. --show adds the matched text
for pattern rules only; a denylist match is never echoed.

Usage:
  check_generality.py                     scan the tracked files of the repository
  check_generality.py --tree DIR          scan every file under DIR (an export stage, a snapshot)
  check_generality.py --staged            scan the staged content (the pre-commit hook)
  check_generality.py PATH ...            scan these files or directories
  check_generality.py --summary           counts by rule and by file instead of every line
  check_generality.py --citations FILE    use this citation list instead of the shipped one
  check_generality.py --add-term CATEGORY read terms from stdin, add their digests to the denylist
Exit 0 when clean, 1 on any finding, 2 on a configuration error.

check.catches:
Protected paths: a learning loop cannot weaken the checks it is judged by.

``src/ravel/data/governance/protected_paths.json`` names the sources and record fields that
judge a run. This module supplies the predicates other packages call:

- ``is_protected(path)``: the path is a protected source (also when it names an installed
  copy under ``.../ravel/...``). The broker is to refuse a write to it.
- ``suppression_rule(text, known_ids=...)``: the do-not-learn rule. It returns the sentences
  that name a target (a check, trap, gate, premise or review-point id, a known bare id, a
  protected file or field, or a weakening flag) and weaken it: remove, skip, stub, patch,
  rewrite, set a threshold, mark as not applicable, call it optional or too strict. A nonempty
  result means the lesson or fix is refused (root-cause analysis and ``knowledge_lessons``).
- ``fix_errors(fix)``: an RCA fix that edits a protected path or field, or suppresses a check.
- ``evaluator_snapshot()`` / ``seal_worker_receipt(receipt, before, after)``: hashes of every
  protected file before and after a worker; a change voids that worker's receipt.
- ``investigator_bundle(results)``: what an RCA investigator sees of a check, its id and
  verdict, never its source.
- ``scan(roots)``: run-time artefacts that write a protected path, carry a suppression lesson
  or leak check source into an investigator bundle. The CLI exits 1 on any finding.

"Never skip check:x" strengthens a check and passes. A sentence that describes when a check
fails passes; one that edits, removes or weakens it is refused. Prose matching screens lessons;
the structural protection is the manifest: ``fix_errors`` refuses an edit to a protected path,
to a protected field, to an ancestor of one, or a new value that carries one. Standard library
only, so CI can run it without the scientific stack.

check.catches:
check:status_packet_resumable -- a status packet regenerated from records alone gives a
byte-identical next work item.

A resumed session reads `current_state.json` (written by `ravel status --write`) to decide what
to do next. That packet must be a pure view of the run's records: regenerating it from a copy of
the run without `current_state.json` must give the same next work item, byte for byte. A
difference means the packet carried state the records do not (or the records changed after it
was written), and a resumed session would act on the wrong item.

The next work item is `{"next_required", "next_instruction"}` serialized canonically
(the shared JSON digest); the copy's path is mapped back to the run's path first.

  python -m ravel.validation.check_status_packet <rundir> [<rundir> ...] [--json]

Exit 0 when every run passes, 1 otherwise. Read-only on the run.

check.catches:
Citations for physics-critical numbers and pinned PDG/Higgs reference contracts.

A number that sets a physical result (a mass, a width, a coupling, a luminosity, a cross section, an
efficiency or a branching ratio) must say where it came from. ``check_document`` walks any JSON-like
document and returns one finding per physics-critical number that has no citation, naming its field path
(for example ``particles[2].mass``). A number that cites a PDG identifier is also compared with the pinned
subset and reported if it disagrees by more than its stated or PDG uncertainty.

    python -m ravel.validation.constants_manifest DOC.json [--pdg]   # exit 1 on any finding
    python -m ravel.validation.constants_manifest --verify-subset    # exit 1 if the subset checksum differs

Typed Higgs tables additionally resolve citation keys, declared absolute uncertainty envelopes and
row-derived ratios. Their acquisition hold and schema live in ``data/knowledge/higgs/``.
``load_higgs_tables`` checks local primary/table pins and rejects synthetic fixtures by default.

The PDG subset and its provenance are ``src/ravel/data/reference/pdg/``: edition, release time, source wheel
and database digests, and the subset's own sha256, all from ``SOURCE.json``.

check.catches:
Pre-shower LHE sanity guard (stdlib-only; reads .lhe or .lhe.gz).

Run this between MadGraph and Pythia — the failure modes it catches are the ones that
otherwise fail SILENTLY downstream (exit 0, plausible-but-wrong yields; see
.claude/rules/madgraph-pythia.md and docs/workflow/checklists/model-cards.md):

  * WRONG GENERATED MASS (--expect-mass PDG:MASS, repeatable): the actual model interface,
    restriction or card loading can differ from the intended spectrum. The
    check reads the FIRST event's particle masses (the ground truth of what was generated)
    and the banner's SLHA MASS block, asserting both within --mass-tol (default 1 GeV).
  * MISSING MODSEL: without `Block MODSEL` (1 1) Pythia keeps internal SUSY off. Measured
    nuance (Pythia 8.31x, this pipeline's certified runs): explicit SLHA DECAY tables WITH
    branching-ratio rows in the banner still decay fine (`SLHA:useDecayTable = on` imports
    them regardless of MODSEL), but particles whose card has width-only DECAY entries (no
    BR rows) rely on Pythia's internal SUSY machinery and will NOT decay -> empty SRs.
    MadGraph does NOT inject MODSEL into the banner — only what the input card carries.
    Default WARN; make it fatal with --require-modsel.
  * WEIGHT SIGN: the first N (--n-events, default 200) events must carry one weight sign
    (mixed signs at LO = misconfiguration; NLO samples legitimately mix — then this guard
    does not apply). Reports sigma from the <init> block.
  * MULTIWEIGHT (<rwgt>/<wgt> tags): single-weight pipelines must run
    `rivet --skip-weights` and generate with use_syst=False (docs/workflow/steps/04-analyze.md).
  * MERGED vs UNMERGED (run-card ickkw): ickkw=1 -> "MERGED (use pythia_shower_merged)";
    plain `pythia_shower` would double-count the ME jets. Absent/0 -> plain shower.

Exit nonzero on any failed assertion; everything is printed as a one-screen report.

A JSON sidecar is ALWAYS written (default <lhe>.lhe_check.json, --json-out overrides) with
the earned verdict + every check — validate_run_state.py's lhe-check-before-shower invariant
gates shower products on exactly this artifact, so a shower that skipped the guard is a
lifecycle FAIL, not a silent omission.

Usage:
  lhe_check.py EVENTS.lhe[.gz] [--expect-mass 1000021:1000] [--expect-mass 1000022:100]
               [--mass-tol 1.0] [--require-modsel] [--n-events 200] [--json-out PATH]

check.catches:
Noise model for a reproduction residual: the size below which a feature is not interpretable.

Every decomposition term is a function of the per-bin signal yields on both sides. Our side
declares each bin's ``sumw2``; the reference declares each bin's ``staterror``. The noise of a
term is the linear propagation of those per-bin variances through the term (a numerical
Jacobian), with bins independent. Where replicas of our claim quantity exist (at least three,
each from a distinct producer-recorded seed), our side of the total residual is the larger of
the propagated noise and the replica scatter's 95% chi-square upper bound, so a few
near-identical replicas cannot shrink it.

Thresholds use one declared false-alarm rate ``alpha``:

- per node, a Sidak multiplier over the number of nodes, so that noise alone crosses some
  node's threshold with probability ``alpha`` across the lattice;
- per scope (all nodes, the nodes of one flavour, or one named signal region), the two-sided ``alpha`` quantile times
  the standard error of a median, ``sqrt(pi/2) * rms(sigma) / sqrt(n)``.

The likelihood term is the claim residual minus the signal-region proxy. Without a joint
estimate of their correlation it takes the uncorrelated sum of both noises, the conservative
choice. Control-region and fit noise reach our result only through replicas, so without them
the likelihood term has no noise budget and no threshold: it is not attributable. The record is
advisory input to ``check:attribution_above_noise``; it does not assert that a feature above
threshold has any particular physical cause.

Output contracts: what each stage must produce before a downstream stage may read it.

A contract is a small JSON object::

    {"name": "detector events", "kind": "delphes-root", "path": "events.root",
     "min_events": 1, "max_events": null, "expected_events": 1000,
     "required": ["Jet.PT", "MissingET.MET"], "weight": "Event.Weight",
     "forbid_all_zero_weights": true, "finite_fraction": 1.0,
     "forbid_constant": ["MissingET.MET"], "reference": {"path": "...", "rel_tol": 1e-9}}

``check(contract, base, snapshot=None)`` returns ``{"passed", "failures", "observed"}``.
Kinds and what they delegate to:

* ``lhe``: ``native_normalization.read_lhe`` (complete document, positive cross section,
  weight census); zero weights fail.
* ``hepmc``: HepMC3/HepMC2 ASCII framing and the event count (plain or gzip).
* ``root-tree`` and ``delphes-root`` (tree ``Delphes``): entries, branch presence, finite
  values, constant branches and the weight sum.
* ``json``: required JSON pointers, finite numbers.
* ``yoda``: ``BEGIN YODA_`` objects and their paths.
* ``saf``: MadAnalysis 5 SAF header and body.
* ``pyhf-workspace``: channels, observations, measurements and version.
* ``file``: a nonempty regular file.

Freshness uses a snapshot taken before the attempt (``snapshot(paths)``): an output that
already existed with the same identity is stale. ``reference`` compares the numeric content
with a reference file and fails a near copy. ``zero_cross_section_status`` classifies a zero
or missing generator cross section: it is confirmed only when the banner states no positive
rate, the log carries a recognised signature and no events were written; anything else is
suspicious and stops the chain.

plot_lint -- the MACHINE GATE behind docs/workflow/checklists/plot-criteria.md.

The gate itself lives in mplhep_style.lint_figure/enforce_lint and runs INSIDE every renderer at
save time (a saved PNG cannot be linted post-hoc -- the check needs the live artists). Renderers
wired in: scan_contour.py (fail-loud, --no-lint to downgrade), overlay_on_data.py,
mass_plane_overlay.py. This CLI exists for two things:

  plot_lint.py --selftest     build a deliberately colliding figure (expect violations) and a
                              clean smart_legend+smart_annotate figure (expect none); exit 0
                              only if BOTH behave. Run under the rivet env:
                              $CONDA run -n rivet python src/ravel/validation/plot_lint.py --selftest

What it checks (mplhep_style.lint_figure docstring is authoritative): legend/boxed-annotation
occlusion of drawn data (fills exempt; bare in-plot feature labels exempt), box-box overlap,
successive tick-label overlap, boxes escaping the canvas.

A requested plot style is a typed constraint, ``figure_spec`` (WALKTHROUGH Δ-Wa4, SG-25):
axis ranges, scales, aspect, binning and label text. ``figure_spec_errors`` checks the spec
itself and ``lint_figure_spec`` checks a live figure against it; a renderer that was given a
spec runs both before saving, beside ``lint_figure``.

check.catches:
Deterministic fit and scan alarms, computed from result records.

Each alarm is a pure function of a result record. It returns check records with
``status`` ``pass``, ``warn`` or ``fail`` and ``computed: true``. The inference
engines store them in ``inference.json`` under ``computed_checks``;
``physics_review`` recomputes them from the retained outputs at acceptance, so
a reviewer or agent cannot overwrite a computed failure. A computed failure
blocks acceptance of a claim scope that requires a scientific check (limits,
measurements, reproductions). An integrity-only diagnostic scope stays
available.

Alarms (``TRIGGERS``):

- ``closure``: chi2/ndf below 0.1 warns (suspiciously good), above 3 fails; any
  closure pull above 5 fails;
- ``fit-triviality``: a chi-square exactly zero with ndf > 0, or a fit that
  returns every parameter at its input value, fails (warns for MC pseudo-data,
  where a perfect fit is expected by construction);
- ``parameter-at-bound``: parameters at or near a fit bound, including the flags
  that other RAVEL engines write (``near_lower_bound``, ``near_upper_bound``,
  ``at_boundary``), warn;
- ``nuisance-pulls``: a constrained pull above 3 warns; an RMS of pulls below
  0.7 with at least five pulls warns (a RAVEL choice: investigate overcoverage);
- ``systematic-dominance``: one source above 80% of the total systematic
  variance warns; a flat (normalisation-only) shift supplied as a shape
  variation in a multi-bin measurement warns;
- ``systematic-selfcheck``: a source with zero impact, or two sources with
  identical shift vectors, fails;
- ``reference-deviation``: a relative deviation above 0.3 from a declared
  well-measured reference fails pending investigation;
- ``goodness-of-fit``: a p-value below 0.05 (outside the 95% toy band) fails; a
  goodness of fit with fixed auxiliary measurements fails (it is refused as the
  reported goodness of fit); the asymptotic fallback is labelled;
- ``excluded-bins``: more than half of the bins excluded from a fit fails;
- ``open-at-edge``: an interval, best fit or contour that touches the hull of
  the evaluated points, or a limit censored at the scan ceiling or floor, fails
  and carries a proposed extension (level lines of declared formulas warn);
- ``validity-status``: a fit or region result without a validity status fails.

Defaults may be changed only with a recorded basis (``review.thresholds``); the
record states the value, its origin and the basis used.

check.catches:
Reproduction-residual decomposition, ``check:attribution_above_noise`` and the RCA trigger.

Input: ``claims/residual_model.json``, a binned signal model on a node lattice. Each node gives
our and the reference's claim quantity (a limit that falls as the signal grows), optional
replicas of ours (each with its seed), declared fingerprint values, and per region the
background, our signal yields with ``sumw2`` and the reference signal yields with ``staterror``.
Regions have a role (``signal`` or ``control``) and an optional flavour.

Authority (``diagnose``): the residual model counts only as the output of a registered stage
receipt from a recognized RAVEL tool (``custody_authority.stage_output``), so our yields,
``sumw2`` and replicas are code-computed. The reference values, reference ``staterror`` and
``alpha`` come only from the noise model pinned by the agreement target that the live
CHECK-IN 1 approval binds; a model that declares other values is refused. The model's nodes
must be exactly the target's compared nodes. ``delivery_errors`` (the CHECK-IN 3 and
``delivery`` gate provider) recomputes every stored decomposition and attribution check from
those custody inputs, so an edited, rehashed record is refused.

Per node, in log space, the claim residual ``total = ln(result / reference)`` splits exactly as

- ``rate``: ``-ln R``, with ``R`` the ratio of our summed signal-region yield to the reference's;
- ``shape``: the stat-only signal-region Asimov proxy ``ln(mu95_SR(ours) / mu95_SR(reference))``,
  computed identically from both sides' yields on the same background, minus the rate term;
- ``likelihood``: the remainder ``total - proxy``. It holds whatever the claim's likelihood does
  that a stat-only signal-region count does not: control-region signal, systematics, the
  statistic's construction.

Rate and shape are also resolved per flavour and per named signal region (scopes
``flavour:<f>`` and ``region:<name>``). Each term is correlated across nodes with the
declared fingerprint variables and with the built-in ``reference_cr_signal_fraction``.
``noise_model`` sets the threshold below which a term is noise. A term is attributed in a scope
only above its threshold; ``check_attribution_above_noise`` refuses any attribution claim that
is not, recomputing each comparison from the record's medians and thresholds. Fingerprint
support uses a Holm correction over every (term, variable) test. When the claim residual exceeds the agreement target's tolerance and its noise,
``open_triggers`` hands one trigger to the RCA ticket and board-epoch producers. While those
modules are absent the trigger is recorded as pending and nothing is called.

The decomposition is a diagnostic ordering of candidate explanations, not a cause.

check.catches:
Conformance of the operation signatures (architecture §2.5.3, Stage 2 row 2-02).

``src/ravel/data/operation_signatures.json`` gives each registered operation a typed
signature: the artifact kinds it consumes and produces, its effects and its evidence-basis
contributions. This module checks that registry:

- every registered mode (science modes and scoped adapters) has an entry;
- each entry is schema-valid and resolves: a science mode names itself and the module its
  adapter resolves to, a scoped adapter is registered, and a command or lifecycle stage
  names an importable module;
- every consumed and produced kind is a known artifact kind with a witness, slot names are
  unique, basis ``passes`` and ``origin_from``/``level_from`` name consumed slots;
- tool names are plain names, and no entry carries a paper or benchmark identifier (R-10).

A witness is a structural predicate for one artifact kind. ``output_errors`` applies the
witnesses of an operation's produced slots to the outputs an adapter wrote, so an adapter
test can show that its outputs are what its signature declares. ``chains`` searches the
registry for operation chains from supplied kinds to a delivered kind, and
``edge_errors`` checks one producer-to-consumer edge.

A signature declares shape, not scientific validity: passing conformance says nothing about
whether an operation's physics is right.

Other packages supply rows through a seam: they write candidate rows to a JSON file
``{operation: entry}`` and run ``python -m ravel.validation.signature_conformance --entries
FILE``; the owner of ``operation_signatures.json`` merges rows that pass.

check.catches:
Bounded exact-law references for a known-background counting experiment.

The ordering is the observed count: CLs(mu;n) = F_(b+mu*s)(n)/F_b(n).
This is not a general profile-likelihood/qtilde calibration or an auxiliary-data
toy construction. Background and signal yields are known, bins are not weighted
observations, and no nuisance, MC or detector uncertainty is manufactured.
"Exact" refers to the Poisson law, not infinite-precision numerical evaluation.

Only the standard library is used. Finite-lattice reports retain each count,
unnormalized probability mass, truncation bounds and numerical allowance.

check.catches:
Runtime HEP tool handbooks: discovery and contract checks.

A handbook is a directory ``src/ravel/data/skills/tools/<tool>/`` holding
``SKILL.md``, a ``references/`` directory and ``references/review.md``. It
ships as package data, so an installed RAVEL finds it with ``handbook_root()``
and an installer copies whole handbook directories into an agent's skills
directory.

The checks, used by ``check_agent_surface``:

- frontmatter: exactly the six Agent Skills keys (name, description, license,
  compatibility, allowed-tools, metadata), RAVEL fields under ``metadata``
  only, ``metadata.ravel-requires-modes`` naming declared science modes;
- budget: the estimated token count of ``SKILL.md`` and of each reference file
  stays within a budget (5000 by default). The estimate is a line proxy: each
  line costs ceil(characters / 4) + 1 tokens;
- pitfalls: every bullet under ``## Pitfalls`` names the RAVEL check that
  catches it (``Caught by `module.function```) or is labelled ``Advisory:``;
- parameters: every ``metadata.ravel-parameters`` entry, and every
  ``operation.field`` path the body mentions, is listed in
  ``data/skills/operation-fields.json``;
- versions: ``metadata.upstream-version`` items (``group:component=version``
  for a toolchain-manifest group, ``pypi:distribution=version`` for a pinned
  Python dependency) match the pins, unless listed in
  ``metadata.ravel-version-unpinned``;
- review record: ``references/review.md`` carries one JSON record naming the
  executable and illustrative code blocks; every ``ravel-block=<id>`` block is
  listed and every listed block exists. ``tests/skills/<name>/`` runs the
  executable ones;
- installed copies: a handbook installed into a skills directory is
  byte-identical to the packaged source;
- collisions (report-only): skill descriptions that overlap strongly.

``availability`` turns a ``ravel doctor`` report (or the older
``native_doctor`` report) into the per-handbook unavailable ledger.

check.catches:
Compare a run's selection acceptance times efficiency with published values.

This is a benchmark point-estimate comparison of the generation, shower, detector
and selection chain. It does not isolate detector efficiency or establish CLs
coverage. Cross-section cancellation requires a consistent generated-process and
normalization basis on both sides.

--sr-reader counter reads A×ε = normalized SR yield / (sigma[fb] * lumi[fb]).
--sr-reader cutflow reads last/first bin. The first bin MUST count the uncut
generated sample; otherwise this is conditional acceptance. This tool cannot
verify that semantic assumption from anonymous bin values. auto chooses by the
YODA object interface (.val() for counter, otherwise .bins() for cutflow).

Published reference lookup uses a 1e-6 GeV numerical tolerance, then local 1-D linear
interpolation across at most --interp-max-span. Interpolation is an approximation
without propagated interpolation uncertainty. A NEAREST reference is retained
for diagnosis but cannot certify a driving region at a different mass point.

Driving regions come from --exclusion (best/near-best expected sensitivity), or
--driving-sr-override. The maximum residual across ALL driving regions controls
the verdict. Missing driving evidence, no driving region, or an unmatched driving
reference means FAIL. Zero selected acceptance against positive published
acceptance is a measured 100% deficit, never missing data. Tails are report-only.

The legacy mu95_impact fields store abs(mine/published - 1), a selection residual
proxy. The separate inverse_signal_limit_shift is 1/ratio - 1, valid only for a
uniform rescaling of the complete signal template with the model otherwise fixed.
Neither quantity is a propagated likelihood uncertainty. MC and published
uncertainties are not propagated, and discrepancy causes remain unresolved.

Exit code 0 means a report was produced; consumers MUST read its PASS/WARN/FAIL
verdict. Input parse/validation failures exit nonzero. Output is Markdown + JSON.

Example:
  validate_cutflow.py --signal SIG.yoda --routine NAME --sigma-pb S --lumi-fb L
      --tables-dir DIR --grid "gluino direct decay" --m-parent 1000 --m-lsp 100
      --srs 2jl,2jm,2jt,4jt,5j,6jm,6jt --out acceptance-certification.md

Plan check for a request plan (``inputs/plan.json``): vocabularies, schemas and typed errors.

A request plan is a directed acyclic graph of registered operations, authored steps,
inputs and open-research envelopes, joined by typed artifact edges, with the claims each
deliverable will make. This module holds the closed vocabularies of the intake
architecture, the reading and plan schemas (written only in the JSON Schema keywords
``validate_task_contract._schema_errors`` evaluates), and ``check``, which returns the plan
errors that do not need full operation signatures. Every error uses the refusal envelope
``{error_class, reason, action_required, suggested_next_operation, evidence_ids}``.

Stage 1 shows and pins the plan; it does not govern. Nothing here approves compute, and
nothing here reads the request's identity context (benchmark, challenge or task labels).

check.catches:
validate_run_state.py -- the lifecycle ORDERING + COMPLETENESS + INVARIANT gate.

Sits between validate_task_contract.py (schema of ONE artifact, the contract) and
verify_pack.py (INTERNAL consistency of whatever artifacts happen to exist, exits 0 on a
run with none). Neither asserts "the declared mode produced its REQUIRED artifacts, in
order, with its cross-stage invariants satisfied" -- this is that gate.

Composition, not duplication: this tool imports validate_task_contract.validate() and runs
it FIRST (a run on an invalid contract cannot mean anything downstream); at the
verification stage it shells out to verify_pack.py and folds its exit into that stage's
result. It does not re-implement either tool's per-artifact shape checks.

Canonical stage order: task_contract, resource_census, trap_sweep, route, figure_contract,
basis_manifest, generation, analysis, statistics, result_pack, verification. Which stages
are REQUIRED/OPTIONAL/N-A/CONDITIONAL for a contract is required_stages() (below), and the
cross-stage INVARIANTS enforce things a per-stage presence check cannot see (R5-before-
limit-ships, resource-census-before-route, the likelihood<->selection pairing gate, ...).

GRANDFATHER (GATE_EPOCH="2026-07-08"): a run dated before the epoch, or lacking an inputs/
dir, is LEGACY -- missing trap_sweep.json / verification.json / resource_census.json
downgrade FAIL to WARN (status "waived-legacy") rather than retro-failing good historical
work. Every VALUE check that CAN run still runs at full severity; new runs get no waiver.

Stdlib-only, read-only, fail-loud.

Usage:
  validate_run_state.py --rundir <dir> [--stage <name>] [--contract <path>] [--strict] [--json]
  validate_run_state.py --rundir <dir> --backfill-plan     # print (don't write) what's missing
  validate_run_state.py --selftest

Exit codes: 0 PASS (WARNs allowed) * 1 required-stage-missing/out-of-order or invariant FAIL
            2 usage / rundir not a directory * 3 contract invalid (validate_task_contract)

check.catches:
verify_pack.py -- mechanical-integrity assertions over a run's artifact JSONs.

The scripted half of Tier A of the ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION PANEL
(docs/workflow/steps/09-verify.md + docs/workflow/checklists/verification-panel.md).
Given a rundir, it finds the artifact JSONs the run carries and asserts their
INTERNAL consistency -- it reads artifacts only, re-runs no physics, modifies
nothing. Checks:

  * every artifact JSON parses (a corrupt artifact is a FAIL);
  * figures.json: every figure file (png + declared pdf) exists on disk;
    captions (what_it_shows) recorded (WARN when not); the embedded figure
    contract's targets fulfilled or WARNed; n_figures bookkeeping;
  * result.json: verdict/limit self-consistency (excluded_obs == (mu95_obs<1),
    mu95_exp == band median, band ordered), pointers resolve on disk,
    n_figures matches figures.json;
  * scan-shaped JSONs (n_planned/n_done/points): coverage bookkeeping
    (n_planned == n_done + n_missing, len(points) == n_done,
    len(missing_tags) == n_missing), unique tags, per-point verdict/band/
    Delta-m self-consistency;
  * scan_manifest.json vs the scan: planned-lattice bookkeeping;
  * sensitivity.json: window keys consistent between background and signals,
    no negative yields;
  * every plot referenced by an artifact JSON or by RESULT.md exists on disk;
  * DEVIATIONS.md exists whenever any artifact JSON carries a 'deviations' key
    or a renorm/rebase-style provenance block (a mid-run protocol adjustment
    that the deviations ledger must mirror -- see checklists/check-ins.md and
    the NUMBER-INTEGRITY rule in checklists/verification-panel.md).

What it CANNOT do (stays with the [agent]): trace numbers quoted in PROSE to
their artifact values, check units, or judge physics -- see the checklist.

Report lines are formatted for direct pasting into the panel's Tier-A section.
Exit 0 = no FAIL (WARNs allowed), 1 = at least one FAIL, 2 = usage error.

Usage:  verify_pack.py <rundir> [--whole-task]
Scoped integrity success does not close the original request. --whole-task also
requires the original-obligation completion input and its actual parent review.

check.catches:
Verify a Rivet routine declares its own DETECTOR SMEARING — the Rivet-path fidelity gate.

This is the Rivet-path analogue of the SimpleAnalysis/Delphes acc×eff certification
(`validate_cutflow.py`): before trusting a Rivet routine's per-SR yields as detector-level, we
confirm the routine itself applies detector smearing/efficiency at the source. A Rivet routine is
detector-level ONLY if it declares Smeared* projections (SmearedJets / SmearedParticles /
SmearedMET) or efficiency-bearing projections — these fold in the experiment's published object
resolution and reco efficiency at the analysis level. A routine with no such projection runs at
TRUTH (particle) level: its objects are generator-truth, so its "acceptance" carries no detector
response. Feeding a BSM signal through a truth-level routine and reading its SRs as if they were
detector-level is the silent failure this gate catches (the degeneracy story: the wrong path makes
acceptance ~2× off because the detector response is simply absent).

WHY a grep gate and not a re-run: the smearing declaration is a STATIC property of the routine
source — `declare(SmearedJets(...), "RecoJets")` etc. It is decidable by reading the .cc, with no
event generation, no Delphes, no Rivet pass. So this gate is cheap (read one file) and deterministic.

The source is scanned AFTER stripping C/C++ comments and string/char literals, and PASS is gated on the
STRUCTURAL declaration `declare(Smeared...(...), "name")` — not a bare `Smeared*` token. So a routine
that merely *mentions* SmearedJets in a `// comment` or a "string literal" is NOT laundered into a
detector-level PASS (the silent false-positive this gate must never produce).

VERDICT (mirrors validate_cutflow.py's three-state authority — PASS / WARN / FAIL):
  - PASS  = detector-level. The routine structurally DECLARES ≥1 Smeared* projection
            (declare(SmearedJets(...), "RecoJets") etc. — SmearedJets / SmearedParticles / SmearedMET).
            Its SR yields fold detector response; the Rivet path is the right path. The note records
            WHICH projections + a best-effort era/experiment (e.g. ATLAS_RUN2) read off the
            smearing/efficiency constant names.
  - WARN  = particle-level only. No structurally-declared Smeared* projection found. The routine either
            carries an efficiency-only projection (efficiency without resolution smearing — a partial
            detector treatment) or has no RECOGNIZED smearing/efficiency projection at all (a custom
            idiom may still be present — this is 'not recognized', not a proof of pure truth level). The
            Delphes-routing advice forks on search-vs-measurement (detector-fidelity.md), read off the
            routine's .info Keywords (search/susy/bsm/exotica) + the id name patterns (_SUSY_/_SUS_/
            _EXOT_/_EXO_):
              · MEASUREMENT/fiducial routine → particle-level BY DESIGN; do NOT run Delphes (the result
                is already unfolded — applying detector effects would be physically wrong). Truth-to-truth.
              · BSM SEARCH with no self-smearing → truth-level search; route to SimpleAnalysis/Delphes
                (tune object efficiencies to the published curves) or mark the result approximate.
            Never read a WARN routine's SRs as detector-level BSM acceptance.
  - FAIL  = the routine source could not be located/read (unusable input: bad --routine/--cc, or the
            .cc is missing under the installed Rivet share). Nothing to verify.

Like validate_cutflow.py the verdict is the authority and is written to JSON; exit code is 0 for any
produced verdict (PASS/WARN/FAIL all exit 0 — the benchmark gate parses the `verdict` field), nonzero
only when arguments are unusable before any verdict can be formed.

Usage:
  verify_smearing.py --routine <ROUTINE> --out <rundir>/outputs/smearing.md
  verify_smearing.py --routine MyRoutine --cc /path/to/MyRoutine.cc --out OUT.md

entries.summary: An Asimov data set represents an expected-data construction at a specified parameter point. Profile-likelihood asymptotic formulae rely on regularity and adequate information; parameter boundaries, sparse counts and non-identifiability can require calibration.
entries.title: Asimov and profile-likelihood assumptions

entries.summary: A CP-odd interference integrand cancels only under a CP-symmetric integration measure, initial-state ensemble, observable bin and acceptance. A CP-even observable alone is insufficient with asymmetric cuts. Distinguish mixing at one vertex from two CP-odd vertices in a complete amplitude.
entries.title: Conditions for CP cancellation

entries.summary: A CP-odd resonance with CP-conserving pseudoscalar production and decay vertices need not have zero interference with the gluon-fusion continuum. CP-odd production times CP-odd decay is not a single CP-odd insertion. The actual helicity amplitudes and accepted observable determine the surviving term.
entries.title: CP-odd resonance and continuum

entries.summary: A total DECAY width does not supply branching fractions or decay channels to a shower. Model, restriction and shower import settings determine which masses and decays are used.
entries.title: Widths and decay branching tables

entries.summary: Fast simulation implements the specific detector card and reconstruction model. Object efficiencies, isolation, overlap removal and working points are not universal, especially for displaced, soft or substructure-dependent objects.
entries.title: Detector card and object efficiency domain

entries.summary: Discovery tests the background-only hypothesis. A local discovery significance and a global significance after searching a parameter range differ. An exclusion contour is not a discovery claim.
entries.title: Discovery significance is a separate quantity

entries.summary: An EFT prediction requires a declared power counting, operator basis and truncation order. The relevant hard invariants and coupling expansion determine validity; a hadron collider beam energy alone is not the expansion parameter for each event.
entries.title: EFT expansion and validity

entries.summary: Four-flavour and five-flavour descriptions allocate heavy-quark contributions differently. Their PDFs, matrix elements, masses and matching prescriptions must form a consistent perturbative prediction.
entries.title: Heavy-flavour scheme and PDF basis

entries.summary: A resonance mass-window cutoff truncates sampled phase space. Matrix-element/parton-shower merging scales and generation cuts also change support and require validation in the requested observable.
entries.title: Resonance support and merging

entries.summary: At energies large compared with the gauge-boson mass, longitudinal-vector amplitudes relate to Goldstone amplitudes with convention-dependent phases and perturbative factors, plus power corrections. Mixing angles, field normalization and vertex signs must be fixed before comparing couplings.
entries.title: Goldstone equivalence and coupling conventions

entries.summary: There is no universal interference K-factor. Signal, background and their cross term receive different perturbative corrections. Taking the geometric mean of signal and background K-factors is an approximation that needs process and kinematic justification, not an identity.
entries.title: Higher-order interference correction

entries.summary: An on-shell colour-singlet spin-1 state cannot couple to two identical on-shell massless vector bosons, including the colour-singlet two-gluon state. Loop corrections do not evade these assumptions. Off-shell partons or additional radiation change the premises. This theorem alone does not forbid decay to massive vector bosons.
entries.title: Landau-Yang constraint

entries.summary: A UFO encodes model parameters, particles, vertices and coupling orders. Successful import does not establish physical consistency, a gauge choice, intended restrictions or the normalization of a supplied coupling.
entries.title: UFO and model convention checks

entries.summary: Small width relative to mass is a necessary guide, not a sufficient error bound for narrow-width factorization. Thresholds, cuts, off-shell tails and interference can spoil a rate-times-branching approximation even for a narrow state.
entries.title: Domain of narrow-width factorization

entries.summary: A reinterpretation needs the observable definition, selection and fiducial domain, rate conventions, correlations and statistical model used for the claimed quantity. A public histogram alone does not supply a likelihood or detector response.
entries.title: Published likelihood and response information

entries.summary: If a supplied full model includes a Standard Model component, adding it to the same Standard Model reference double counts that component. Form the model-minus-reference contribution using the same fiducial definitions and retain correlations from shared events and shared nuisance sources.
entries.title: Reference subtraction and covariance

entries.summary: Signed interference and model-minus-reference streams can have a nearly cancelling sum of weights. Scaling each stream to a total rate by its own sumw is invalid unless that rate and denominator describe that same stream. Preserve the generator-defined absolute integration normalization, exposure, sumw2 and covariance between correlated streams.
entries.title: Signed and difference weight normalization

entries.summary: A single-charge cross section and a charge-summed cross section describe different process populations. Proton PDFs can give unequal charge-conjugate rates; multiplying a single-charge rate by two requires evidence.
entries.title: Single-charge versus charge-summed rates

entries.summary: For exclusion without a prescribed statistic RAVEL uses 95% CLs. A prescribed statistic, confidence region or credible interval remains the primary requested quantity. CLs is a modified frequentist ratio of tail probabilities; it is not a discovery p-value or Bayesian probability.
entries.title: Requested statistic and CLs default

entries.summary: For an on-shell two-body decay use the complete amplitude and Lorentz-invariant phase space, average over initial spin when appropriate and sum final states. An identical-final-state symmetry factor belongs to the final-state phase space, not to identical incoming beams.
entries.title: Tree-level two-body width

entries.summary: An unfolded measurement inherits response and regularization assumptions from its reference model. A new resonance or altered event composition can change migrations; agreement with the tabulated bins does not validate those response assumptions.
entries.title: Unfolding-model validity

entries.summary: Expected selected yield is luminosity times the cross section for the declared event population times selection efficiency. Branching fractions and filter efficiency enter once if they are not already included. Convert pb and inverse fb consistently: their product carries a factor of 1000.
entries.title: Cross section, luminosity, branching and filter basis

entries.summary: Report an inclusive bump hunt, the frozen reference method, and a truth-supervised oracle ceiling in separate information columns. Inclusive uses efficiency one and no training. The oracle sees information unavailable to a real search and is never an available rival or a member of the search maximum. An independent labelled training pool can define that ceiling when search data contain only background. An idealized anomaly reference can use truth-clean sidebands in a synthetic study; label this additional information. Unsupervised scores still need a justified background estimate and calibrated inference after learning. Compare actual training and epoch counts as well as shared limits; report wall and CPU actuals and per-family configuration counts. Report every declared signal family, strength, null result, insensitive result and failure. Do not average only favourable signals. The receipt's information labels must survive every downstream table and figure.
entries.title: Baseline information and budget

entries.summary: A learned cut changes the inference distribution even when Pearson correlation is small or vanishes. Check sideband separability, efficiency versus sideband bin at every working point, and spurious structure on an independent background-only reference. Use group-aware fold isolation. The current permutation implementation requires one independent row per group; its mean/quadratic moment diagnostic is finite, not a universal independence certificate. Compare the reference's feature and resonance dependence in the sidebands. A mismatched reference cannot certify spurious-signal closure. A quadratic proxy can agree between sidebands while producing a central excess. A shift confined to the signal region is invisible to sideband-only checks. Therefore a null sideband result without a suitable reference leaves the study limited. A learned correction to a detector observable requires a human bespoke_calibration decision and an independently justified correction operation; do not derive it opportunistically to pass a check.
entries.title: Selection sculpting and reference controls

entries.summary: Partition signal groups into disjoint injection and evaluation pools. Exact-count weighted draws use no replacement within a sampling. Retrain every fold, transform and initialization at each strength and sampling. Freeze the complete model set before its one evaluation access. Report signal efficiency separately at every data efficiency and strength, including zero acceptance. Never transfer efficiency between strengths. Declare the median metric before results. An injected-limit prescription using max(limit, injected) requires its monotonicity assumption to be established; this executor does not implement an exclusion-limit prescription or infer a limit from classifier efficiency. Strong injection can saturate efficiency and weak injection can be insensitive; neither outcome disappears from the report. Whole-procedure null toys repeat the learning, thresholds and fit. Failed toys count as extreme and p cannot resolve below 1/(N+1). Conditional injection-response intervals describe randomized draws and folds on fixed supplied pools and the supplied toy ensemble; they do not count samplings or seeds as new independent data and do not establish power over a population of experiments.
entries.title: Injection, evaluation and calibration

entries.summary: Pin datasets, ordered features, model configurations, executed code, split rules and placement before CHECK-IN 1. Hash and explicit modes use three separately pinned files. Cross-fitting hashes groups and rotates validation folds; an event's scoring ensemble excludes that group from training, validation and transform fitting. Test exposure is recorded before evaluation. A zero-read failed reservation can retry; a spent exposure cannot. Inner initializations select by validation loss. Outer seeds measure initialization variation with folds fixed; separate salts measure fold variation. Report both, not a confidence band over independent events. Equal trained-arm budgets mean the same training opportunities, epoch and patience caps, and wall ceiling; report CPU actuals. Inclusive has zero training. Preflight derives region/fold counts from precision and prices every training from a pinned smoke measurement. Missing counts, unpriced campaigns and a changed workload need replanning. Preserve every candidate history, failed toy and zero-acceptance result.
entries.title: Training governance

entries.summary: Classification between mixtures can order signal against background when the component distributions are shared and the fractions differ. Equal fractions give no identifiable signal ordering. Region labels are not signal truth. Declare signal and sideband edges, sideband weights and all feature dependencies before training. The resonance variable and its derivatives are forbidden features. Equal sideband weighting balances their contributions; population weighting retains a falling spectrum's imbalance. Neither choice proves independence or removes a general linear feature trend. A per-region marginal quantile transform is fitted on training folds only and pooled only across declared coordinates. It does not establish independence of joint feature distributions and can change under signal contamination. Rank scores on the declared held-out signal-region reference, average validation rotations, then rerank. Apply one data-efficiency threshold over the entire range. Per-bin thresholds hide sculpting. Validate first in simulation, then an independent or orthogonal control region spanning the full gap, then decide unblinding. Overlapping windows share events and require trials accounting.
entries.title: Mixtures, weak labels and ranks

entries.summary:
Signal cross sections from pinned published tables under an explicitly selected convention.

The registry (``data/cross_sections/registry.json``) lists the LHC SUSY Cross
Section Working Group tables (NNLL-fast and Resummino) with their production
state basis, collision energy, perturbative order, PDF set, scale choice,
source URL, citation and sha256. A request names the basis, the energy and the
convention (order, PDF, scale). The service then:

* returns the published value at a node, or interpolates log sigma linearly in
  log mass between nodes (bilinear in the log masses on two-dimensional grids);
* never extrapolates and never substitutes another convention, order or flat
  correction factor when the selected table is missing;
* rescales by a declared number of degenerate states only where the table
  records the physics rule that allows it;
* sums charge-conjugate states only from tables of the same convention.

An MG5-computed cross section is a separate source with its own convention
(``mg5_record``); a correction factor between two records is accepted only
when they describe the same basis, energy, masses, charge and state count.
entries.title: physics/cross_sections.py

entries.summary:
RAVEL construction context for each AgentRivet role, and text feedback for repairs.

A brief is a small JSON document presented beside an original role's messages.
It carries what RAVEL knows and the upstream roles lack: the routine name the
build will require, the HEPData tables with their binning, the typed analysis
specification with its ambiguity record, the normalization contract, RAVEL's
Rivet authoring guidance and review checklist, and the latest construction
check of the draft under work. Upstream messages are never edited.
entries.title: workflow/agentrivet_brief.py

entries.summary:
Full supplied SModelS coverage -> existing located knowledge/research inputs.

entries.summary:
Write and check a run's physics trap sweep (``inputs/trap_sweep.json``).

The sweep follows docs/workflow/checklists/physics-traps.md. The host records a
verdict for every trap T1..T12; this tool writes the record the lifecycle
validator reads and checks it with that same validator.

    python -m ravel.workflow.trap_sweep write --rundir RUN --input verdicts.json [--replace]
    python -m ravel.workflow.trap_sweep validate --rundir RUN [--require-discharged] [--json]

Input for ``write``::

    {"verdicts": [{"id": "T1", "hit": false, "evidence": "..."},
                  {"id": "T8", "hit": true, "evidence": "...", "consequence": "...", "flag_number": 3},
                  ...one row for each of T1..T12],
     "escalations": [{"id": "T5", "reason": "..."}],
     "obligations": [{"trap": "T8", "obligation_kind": "...", "artifact": null, "status": "PENDING"}]}

``escalations`` and ``obligations`` are optional. A hit needs a ``consequence``
and either a positive ``flag_number`` or an escalation row. Every hit except T3
and T9 (handled by the basis manifest) gets a PENDING obligation when none is
supplied. Exit codes: 0 success/PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 input or write error.

You are the scientific critic, registered as `physics_critic`. Examine the supplied

read producer RESULT.md or explore the run tree. Build your checks from the review
obligations the caller supplies with the packet. They come from the requested
quantity and the scientific contracts the request plan applies
(`python -m ravel.workflow.critic_obligations --plan <run>/inputs/plan.json`):
each claim kind adds the checks its quantity needs, each planned stage adds its
invariants, and provenance, scope and units apply to every review. Exclusion checks
(the declared statistic, resolved threshold crossings, the analysis's own
statistical model, no discovery phrasing) apply only to an exclusion claim. Locate
the evidence for each obligation through the packet index. If the caller supplies no
obligations, derive them the same way from the pinned plan and say so. A missing
obligation for the requested quantity is a finding.

Separate an unsupported result claim from an untested research proposal. Missing
prior literature or efficacy evidence is not, by itself, a defect in a proposal
to investigate that very uncertainty. For exploratory decisions, make criticism
productive: identify a competing mechanism, useful revision or discriminating
experiment. Review actual results strictly within their declared scope. A failed
hypothesis can be a successful and informative diagnostic experiment.

Use `docs/workflow/reference/physics-review.md`. The caller must give you a fresh
context without the producer transcript, headline, preferred interpretation or
other reviewers' verdicts. It retains the packet creation manifest digest outside
the packet and verifies each supplied artifact through the bounded
`ravel review-context read` reader with that digest. Read only indexed packet copies
and supplied methodology references. Do not read RESULT.md or explore the run tree.

tool and this prompt do not establish an OS sandbox or authenticated reviewer
independence; the caller must enforce the access scope.

Check executed settings and successful receipts, exposure and complete channels,
units and normalization, observed/expected roles, process and charge/flavour
basis, detector/selection definition, source applicability and precision. Preserve
paired event IDs, original weights and correlation groups. Missing reference
covariance is unresolved, never zero. Separate integrity, calibration, diagnostic
agreement and publication reproduction. A central value, JSON pass or aggregate
agreement cannot establish those other claims.

At consequential or unsupported steps, ask why the supporting assertion justifies
its parent. Record brief public scientific rationales and reviewed links, not
private reasoning traces. Descend only when conflict, novelty, consequence or a
missing premise warrants it. End at a pinned observation, source, invariant or
user requirement, or return a specific evidence/experiment request. No mandatory
seven-level essay. A structural decision-case pass does not prove entailment.

On a successor cycle, inspect every inherited factual closure obligation. If its
ID/evidence is absent, request it before accepting; never guess or drop it. The

`actor_id`, `verdict` (`accept`, `send_back`, `stop`), `summary`, `findings`,

evidence, with all required inherited IDs in `closes`. Each blocking finding needs

source identities for evidence, not the packet copy filename. Make uncertainty
and evidence requests explicit; do not invent a fix or overstate the supported scope.

protocol: Before certifying a fitted or selected result, run the input-closure check against its pinned certifying reference. A reference that fitted or selected the candidate cannot certify it; stale or incomplete provenance cannot establish independence.
Independently test the evidence and every inherited closure obligation; an unexecuted repair remains untested.
Check every input, required output and inherited obligation against the pinned contract. Preserve failed and unresolved evidence.
Only new_receipt, code_check or a typed discriminating-test request can block. Ask for the cheapest test that could invalidate the claim. Cited claims and opinions remain advisory.
Report public rationales and located evidence. Never accept your own work, widen approval or erase an unresolved obligation.

You are the skeptical verifier, registered as `skeptical_verifier`. The caller
supplies your distinct declared actor ID and prospective policy. Use
`docs/workflow/reference/physics-review.md`.

Start fresh with the verifier packet only, without producer/improver transcripts
or other reviewers' verdicts. The caller retains its creation manifest digest
outside the packet and verifies indexed content through `ravel review-context
read` before presenting evidence. Read only indexed copies and supplied methodology
references. Request a bounded source-pinned witness for omitted large files. This
prompt and Read tool are guidance, not an OS sandbox or an authenticated independence
guarantee; the caller must enforce the access scope.

On an initial cycle, independently examine evidence and applicability of the named
scope; an improver is unnecessary when no repair is needed. On a repair cycle,
use `verification_scope`: test each listed finding against old/admitted setting
hashes, exact stage specifications, fresh receipts, new outputs, rechecked
criteria and held-fixed controls. `fresh_attempts_available` false means admission
is a proposal, not executed repair evidence. Never close an execution-dependent
objection before successor evidence exists.

Try to invalidate the repair's discriminating prediction, not merely confirm its
explanation. Check paired event/weight completeness and covariance, population
and data-use separation, exposure/channels, observed/expected roles, normalization,
precision and unchanged controls. Equal aggregate yields can hide shape changes;
missing reference covariance remains unresolved. Pass labels and hashes do not
prove physics or source authority. A narrow repair does not certify the whole analysis.

For disputed support, audit brief public assertion/rationale links until they end
in a pinned source, observation, invariant or explicit requirement. Unknown
assumptions and unsupported links become specific evidence/experiment requests.
Do not demand fixed-depth prose or private reasoning traces.

Return a proposed strict review request: `role`, `actor_id`, `verdict` (`accept`,
`send_back`, `stop`), `summary`, `findings`, `closes`, and `claim_scope`. Name each
inherited finding ID closed and its fresh evidence. New blocking findings need
`id`, `summary`, located `evidence` (`path`, `location`), `check_ids`,
`required_paths`, and `required_stages` within policy. Use packet source identities
for evidence paths. Preserve remaining objections and scope limits. Accept only
what the evidence supports.

Do not modify files, execute compute, submit your own review or issue user GO.

For `ravel judgment` repair-design packets, return scientific_repair_design_review with adequate_for_bounded_test, unresolved or contradicted. This assesses the exact prepared intervention and its prospective observations, not observed scientific closure. Keep verdict/scope/proposal null and closes/findings empty. A later successful successor requires a separate scientific_review of raw executed evidence and all inherited rechecks.
See `docs/workflow/reference/scientific-judgment.md` for the ordinary callable transitions.

entries.summary: **Signal–SM interference.** The BSM amplitude shares initial+final state with a large SM amplitude → the observable signature is peak–dip (or pure shape distortion), NOT a bump. Classic: a heavy (pseudo)scalar A/H→tt̄ near the pair-production threshold against SM tt̄; W′→tb̄ vs s-channel top. A declared power-law coupling scaling (g/g₀)^k, or a morphing basis without its lower orders, on a final state shared with an SM amplitude of the same structure assumes the interference away. | Shared initial and final states with a Standard Model amplitude, including a loop-induced channel? Are interference and relative phase relevant in the signal window? If a power-law scaling or reduced morphing basis is declared on such a final state, run a σ-only probe with the SM amplitude on and report the fitted lower-order fraction. | A naive σ×BR bump limit is invalid. Inspect interference-aware published results or construct a compatible coherent signal-plus-background prediction and statistical model through current operations. Preserve signed interference, relative phase, response and uncertainty requirements. Withhold unsupported limit claims while recovering or testing missing inputs; a sensitivity diagnostic does not complete a requested constraint. Never overlay a Breit-Wigner and call it a limit. |
entries.title: T1

entries.summary: **Non-standard reconstruction objects.** The analysis selects on objects the fast chain doesn't model: groomed fat-jet substructure (τ_N, SoftDrop mass), b/τ/top taggers at specific WPs, soft tracks, displaced vertices, AD scores. | List every selection variable in the paper's object section; mark each as {Delphes-standard, derivable at particle level, requires published efficiency, unavailable}. | Derivable → particle-level proxy with fidelity labels (Option C precedent: CMS A→BC, ATLAS AD trials); published per-object efficiencies → fold them; neither → the block, with the object named. Tagger WPs NEVER guessed — published (ε_sig, ε_bkg) or flagged. |
entries.title: T10

entries.summary: **Spectrum-card override + decay-table traps (generation-side).** Mass/mixing inputs depend on the imported model and restriction; MSOFT/HMIX presence alone does not establish an override; width-only DECAY tables (no BR rows) → Pythia imports nothing → undecayed sparticles → empty SRs, exit 0. | `lhe_check.py --expect-mass` BEFORE showering, always; card diff against the model-cards recipe. | Fix the card, never the symptom; the gate is mandatory (steps 03); catalogue C1 is the worked case. |
entries.title: T11

entries.summary: **Production-mode PDF sensitivity.** b-initiated processes (bbA/bbH), photon-initiated production, or heavy-flavor-enhanced modes: the default LO proton PDF choice moves σ at the tens-of-% level, and 4F vs 5F scheme changes the process definition itself. | Is any initial-state parton b/γ, or the paper explicit about 4F/5F or a special PDF? | Match the paper's scheme+PDF (declare it in the basis manifest); if unmatched, quote the σ spread as a flagged uncertainty, not silently. |
entries.title: T12

entries.summary: **Long-lived / displaced decays.** Any new state with cτ ≳ 0.1 mm (check Γ in the card/model!): prompt-object reconstruction (vanilla Delphes, standard SA objects) silently returns ~zero or nonsense efficiency — exit 0, empty/false SRs. | Compute cτ = ħc/Γ for every BSM state in the decay chain; any in [0.1 mm, 10 m]? Analysis mentions displaced/disappearing/DV/dE-dx objects? | The standard chain is OFF the table. Route: efficiency-map folding (the analysis's published per-object efficiency maps on HEPData resources — the LLP-recast standard), or the honest block. Detector_mode label changes; flag the cτ. |
entries.title: T2

entries.summary: **Simplified-model purity broken at the target point.** Published limits assume a pure state / fixed BRs (pure higgsino, 100% BR); the requested plane breaks it (M₁=M₂ & tanβ=50 → MIXED wino–bino–higgsino: masses, σ, BRs, AND A×ε all move). | Does the target parameter plane hold the published model's stated assumptions (purity, BR=1, degeneracies) at EVERY point of the requested range? | Per-point spectrum calculation (mixing matrices) + σ×BR re-weighting BEFORE any limit mapping; A×ε revalidation where the kinematics shift; basis manifest (P2) mandatory. Escalate with the decomposition — this is never a silent proceed. |
entries.title: T3

entries.summary: **Trigger/reconstruction floors vs the mass range under study.** The range extends below (or between) the analyses' trigger thresholds or boosted-regime floors (diboson resonances below the boosted-jet mass regime; low-mass dijets vs HLT floors; low-energy anomaly windows). | Compare the analysis's trigger + leading-object thresholds against the signal's characteristic pT/mass at the studied parameter values. | "Coverage is sparse/absent here" is a FIRST-CLASS answer — evidence it (thresholds vs kinematics), name the nearest covering analyses (TLA/ISR-assisted/prescaled), and deliver the coverage map instead of forcing a limit from an insensitive search. |
entries.title: T4

entries.summary: **Shape-fit statistical paradigm.** The analysis uses a functional form or templates across a spectrum. Its likelihood, correlations and background treatment determine the statistical operation. | Read the paper's statistics section: "background parameterization", "fit function", "template/profile over the spectrum" vs "signal regions + yields". HEPData: no per-SR yields table is a strong hint. | Inspect the published/native likelihood and current binned, continuous or custom fit construction contracts. Recover the complete domain, background and nuisance model, correlations and applicable validation. A shape label is not a blanket refusal. An incompatible counting substitute remains invalid; hold the dependent inference while constructing and qualifying the appropriate fit, preserving the original requested scope. |
entries.title: T5

entries.summary: **ISR-driven compressed-spectrum acceptance.** Δm ≪ m: everything visible comes from ISR recoil, so A×ε hangs on generator ISR modeling, merging choice, and tune — a 2× yield error with exit 0. | Δm/m ≲ 0.1 anywhere in the plane? SRs cut on ISR proxies (R_ISR, pT(jet1)/MET, soft leptons)? | ME/PS treatment is a DECLARED choice (merging or matched ISR jet in the process definition); run-card jet cuts audited against the anchor σ (P4 — the ptj1min incident lived here); expect the fast-sim floor to be worst here and SAY so in the deliverable. |
entries.title: T6

entries.summary: **Dark-sector shower under-specification.** Hidden-valley / semi-visible-jet asks: Λ_d, N_c/N_f, dark-hadron spectrum, r_inv, decay portal — papers under-specify, Pythia HV defaults silently fill the gaps → wrong jet substructure and MET with no error. | Are ALL HV parameters the paper used recoverable (paper, aux material, authors' cards on HEPData/GitHub)? List each one: source or ASSUMED. | Every assumed parameter is a numbered flag; a truth-level validation gate vs any published gen-level distribution runs BEFORE detector simulation or scans; sensitivity-only labels until validated. |
entries.title: T7

entries.summary: **Wide resonances (Γ/m ≳ 5%).** Narrow-width approximation breaks: σ×BR factorization degrades, the low-mass PDF-enhanced tail grows, signal shape morphs across the fit window, interference (T1) grows with Γ. | Γ/m over the studied range (strongly coupled mediators can reach tens of percent); does the published analysis quote limits only for narrow widths? | Evaluate shape and acceptance at each requested width using new generation or applicable, independently reviewed coherent amplitude reuse/full matrix-element reweighting. Check phase-space support, effective statistics, interference, acceptance and tail/Breit-Wigner cutoff conventions. Generate new samples when reuse cannot cover the required support or precision. Normalization-only rescaling of a narrow template is invalid. A narrow-only published limit cannot directly supply broad-width constraints; qualify the appropriate model and fit. |
entries.title: T8

entries.summary: **σ×BR / coupling convention mismatches.** HVT model A vs B (g_V), single-charge vs charge-summed EWKino grids, one-flavor vs summed sleptons, σ×BR vs σ×BR×A — the silent factor-of-N class. | Before ANY published-limit comparison: write both sides' basis manifest (P2). The WG-grid charge/flavor conventions are in `.claude/rules/statistics.md`. | Transform onto ONE declared basis and record it in the artifact (`model_basis` block precedent); the identity check where available (on-contour UL/σ_model = 1). k<1 or a factor ≈2/N is a convention smell, not physics (B-class incidents). |
entries.title: T9

entries.summary: Interference between CP-even and CP-odd scalar amplitudes integrates to zero in CP-even observables such as the angle-integrated four-lepton mass. It can be nonzero in angular or CP-odd observables.
entries.title: cp-even-cp-odd-interference-in-even-observables

entries.summary: A CP-odd scalar produced in gluon fusion interferes with the gluon-fusion diboson continuum in general; the interference is not zero by symmetry.
entries.title: cp-odd-continuum-interference

entries.summary: No universal higher-order K-factor applies to interference terms; the correction for signal, background and interference can differ.
entries.title: interference-k-factor

entries.summary: An on-shell colour-singlet spin-1 state cannot be produced from two on-shell gluons (Landau-Yang). A Z'-like vector is produced through quark-antiquark annihilation at leading order. The theorem does not forbid its decay to two massive Z bosons.
entries.title: landau-yang

entries.summary: A signal rate scaled as a pure power of a coupling presumes incoherent addition; a final state shared with a Standard Model amplitude of the same structure also carries interference terms of lower order in the coupling.
entries.title: power-law-signal-scaling

entries.summary: Adding a model prediction that already contains the Standard Model to a published Standard Model baseline counts the Standard Model twice.
entries.title: reference-double-counting

entries.summary: Analysis routines that scale histograms by cross section over the sum of weights mis-normalise signed or difference weight streams (interference, model minus reference).
entries.title: signed-weight-normalisation

entries.summary: A selection, calibration or normalization chosen for agreement with observed data biases any later inference that uses the same data region.
entries.title: tuning-to-observed-data

entries.summary: An unfolded measurement is tested for deviations from its unfolding model only up to some size. Large resonant deviations can be biased by the unfolding.
entries.title: unfolding-validity
